purpose: Known-motion validation of mean local warp removal, plus an oracle matched-blur diagnostic
repeat_continuation: Combined runner exited 143 after 13 repeat conditions; the missing texture/weighted_motion_blur case completed separately with seed 9018.
validation: 9 targeted tests passed, including CPU/CUDA trace parity; sharpened implementation and recipe match the previously verified PlanetaryTools harness.

primary.global_shift: Oracle best constant-vector fit to true displacement over scene mask, independently per frame
limits: Synthetic composed shears are not a full atmospheric or planetary rotation model.
Reference is fixed; Saturn source contains its existing reference texture and noise.
Noise is independent Gaussian with an illustrative amplitude, not a fitted sensor model.
Generation uses cubic interpolation; reconstruction uses the production bilinear sampler.
Blur is applied before geometric motion; reference does not share the extra blur.
All frames are retained; only the explicitly weighted case changes scalar contributions.
Image RMSE uses a noiseless oracle with identical reconstruction interpolation.
No photometric normalization or output smoothing is applied.
Sharpened errors compare the same two-step nonlinear recipe with the noiseless oracle; they are not noise-only estimates.

conclusions: Mean residual removal improves the symmetric-reference tests but distorts true persistent deformation, even when global translation is preserved.
The second noise seed confirms the regression; weighted frame selection can also make the true mean residual nonzero.
Known-blur templates lower clean-image error in all ten tested conditions but barely improve full-mask Saturn displacement error.
Known-blur templates slightly worsen all five Saturn sharpened image-error comparisons; this is not a demonstrated solution to the real-capture sharpening issue.
No new normalization, output smoothing, or production algorithm change.
